clue.text: Put a damper on party craze around university

indicators.note: around tells you the party and craze together surround the university's letter

parts.note: a disco is a dance party
a rage is a fashionable craze, as in all the rage

explanation.surface: Someone spoils a fad for partying that is sweeping the campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the container signal; the surface makes 'party craze' one thing, but it is two separate pieces side by side, wrapped about the university's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to dampen someone's enthusiasm is to dishearten or deter them.

clue.text: Fool's intelligence

definitions.meaning: an informal word for a stupid person
slang for inside information, as in getting the lowdown on something

explanation.definitionFit: Two slang senses of one word: a simpleton, and inside information passed on to someone.

clue.text: Puts foot down over partner's issue

parts.note: someone who puts a foot down steps
over can mean on, as in a blanket laid over the bed

explanation.surface: Somebody takes a firm line about a problem their other half has.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' is the trap: in the surface it is a problem, but here it means offspring, the child a partner brings to a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword-only sense of issue as children: the boy your spouse had before you is this relation to you.

clue.text: No place for insider trading?

parts.note: insider trading is read literally as buying and selling done indoors, so this is where dealing happens outside under the sky

explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical description: stalls set up outdoors are where nobody trades inside.

clue.text: Improve text in part for revered actor

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A script is being polished, in one role, for a much admired performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to edit a piece of writing for publication is to tidy and correct it.

clue.text: Splendid stuff, contents of house

parts.note: to stuff yourself is to gorge on food

indicators.note: contents of asks for the inside letters of the next word, leaving off its first and last

explanation.surface: An admirer praises the lovely things found inside a home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuff' reads as a noun for belongings but is a verb here, to overeat; 'contents of' takes the inner letters of 'house'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something magnificent or dazzlingly beautiful.

clue.text: Hands over in exchange

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for hands is read from its last letter to its first

parts.note: paws is a jocular word for hands, as in keep your paws off

explanation.surface: Something is passed across as part of a trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands over' looks like a single verb meaning gives; split it, and 'over' turns PAWS round.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to trade one thing for another.

clue.text: Piece of furniture that now has ends replaced

indicators.note: the ends meant are the outer letters of the two-word phrase: the first letter of that and the last letter of now
replaced says each of those outer letters gives way to the other, so the pair trade places

explanation.surface: An old cabinet has just had its side panels renewed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has ends replaced' swaps the outer letters of the phrase 'that now': its opening T and closing W change places.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a stand of open shelves for displaying ornaments, popular in Victorian homes.

clue.text: Its pies are demolished

indicators.note: demolished means knocked to pieces, so the letters before it are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: these three words supply all the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Somewhere sells pastries that get greedily wolfed down.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: 'demolished' rearranges the first three words, and also means eaten up.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: a cake shop is a place whose pastries get eagerly eaten.

clue.text: Reject even pieces of perfect finish as fake

indicators.note: throwing out the second, fourth and sixth letters leaves the odd-numbered ones of the next word

parts.note: to finish is to end

explanation.surface: A dealer dismisses flawlessly lacquered items, level in tone, as forgeries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reject even pieces of' drops alternate letters of 'perfect', keeping the odd ones; 'fake' is a verb here, to sham.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a verb: to feign or put on a false show.

clue.text: Giving off some heat in angry words about support in retreat

indicators.note: about tells you the angry words go round the outside of the other piece

parts.note: a rant is an angry tirade

indicators.note: a retreat is a going back, so the word for support is read from end to start

parts.note: to aid is to support or help

explanation.surface: A row over backing for withdrawing troops gets rather warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal and 'in retreat' turns the support round to give DIA; the surface suggests an army falling back.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: a heater of this kind glows and emits warmth.

clue.text: Mess is something setter might make a meal of

definitions.meaning: British slang for a muddle or botched job

definitions.text: something setter might make a meal of
definitions.meaning: a setter is a breed of hound, so this is literally its morning feed

explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom for a shambles, and literally what a hound eats first thing in the morning.

clue.text: They help locate data doctor has, e.g., in screen

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters after it are rearranged

parts.note: these four words supply the thirteen letters, punctuation ignored

explanation.surface: Tools for finding records, like one a medic keeps on a monitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' is a verb, not a medic: it rearranges HAS EG IN SCREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Google and its rivals are the tools people use to find information online.

clue.text: How urgently needed equipment should be stored, as bicycles must be fixed

definitions.text: How urgently needed equipment should be stored

indicators.note: something that must be fixed needs putting right, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: these two words supply the ten letters

explanation.surface: Vital kit ought to be kept somewhere handy, the way bikes get secured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be fixed' rearranges AS BICYCLES; in the surface 'fixed' means fastened or repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb answering how: within easy reach, so it can be got at quickly.

clue.text: Player not on side making some indecent remark

indicators.note: making some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A footballer caught offside lets slip a rude comment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not on side' suggests offside, but it means not on the wing: a position in the middle of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A position in rugby or football played in the middle rather than on the flank.

clue.text: Newspaper articles about British lie getting heated, naturally

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
A is the indefinite article
THE is the definite article

explanation.surface: Press pieces on a falsehood told in Britain are stirring up fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lie' looks like a falsehood but means recline; 'about' wraps A and THE round B.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: to stretch out and be warmed by the sky's own rays rather than a heater.

clue.text: British, in disorderly era, give overlong sentences?

indicators.note: in tells you the letter for British sits inside the rearranged letters
disorderly means in a mess, so the letters of the two words after it are rearranged

explanation.surface: In a lawless age, UK judges hand out excessive jail terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the British letter inside VERIAGE, which 'disorderly' makes; 'sentences' are strings of words, not prison terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: wordiness, prose that uses far more words than needed.

clue.text: Couple found in stormy Med taken on board

indicators.note: found in tells you the word for a couple sits inside the rearranged letters
stormy weather throws things about, so the three letters after it are rearranged

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as in a brace of pheasants

explanation.surface: Two people adrift in rough seas are rescued by a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' places the couple inside EMD, which 'stormy' makes; 'on board' hints at a ship but the phrase means accepted.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an idea accepted and adopted willingly.

clue.text: Fish with line, rod and weights

parts.note: a barbel is a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: An angler's tackle: a catch, plus everything on the end of the pole.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as angling gear; the definition is a weightlifter's bar with discs on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: a metal bar loaded with heavy discs for lifting.

clue.text: Variety of alpine, one at home in mountains

indicators.note: a variety of something is a different form of it, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: this word supplies the six letters

explanation.surface: A kind of rock plant that thrives at high altitude.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a native of the Himalayan country that holds Everest.

clue.text: Cut in a game of cards

parts.note: bridge is a card game for four players

explanation.surface: A player splits the pack during a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' suggests cutting the deck; here it means shorten.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to shorten a text by trimming it.

clue.text: Black bird of prey hunting dog

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an eagle is a large raptor

explanation.surface: A dark raptor is out chasing a hound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hunting' seems to be what the bird is doing to the dog, but it describes the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a small hound bred for tracking hares.

clue.text: Hit by wave, one labours on regardless

parts.note: to strike is to hit
a breaker is a wave crashing on the shore

explanation.surface: A swimmer battered by a big roller keeps struggling forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'labours on' looks like plodding along; it means carrying on working while colleagues have walked out.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: someone who keeps working during an industrial stoppage, defying the union.

clue.text: Don't run very fast for a left-winger

definitions.meaning: an instruction to go at a jog rather than a sprint
British slang for a Trotskyist, a follower of the Russian revolutionary

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to jog along gently, and British slang for a far-left socialist.

clue.text: Drink for one who's ill with complaint, with meal to follow

indicators.note: with meal to follow says the meal comes second, after the complaint

parts.note: a beef is a grumble or grievance
tea is the British late-afternoon or early-evening meal

explanation.surface: A patient with an ailment gets a beverage now and food afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' reads as an illness but is a grumble; 'with ... to follow' sets the order.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: a hot meaty broth traditionally given to invalids in Britain.

clue.text: More imposing regal father and daughter

parts.note: GR, George Rex, is the royal cipher of King George VI, the father
taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the cipher of his daughter Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: A king and a princess, each looking statelier than the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regal' covers both: the royal ciphers of George VI (GR) and his daughter Elizabeth II (ER), joined by 'and' as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparative synonym: statelier, more magnificent.

clue.text: University that might be picked by expert

definitions.meaning: an Ivy League college in New Haven, Connecticut

definitions.text: that might be picked by expert
definitions.meaning: a well-known brand of cylinder lock, which a skilled burglar could pick

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one name: an American Ivy League college and a famous make of door lock.

clue.text: Bitterness from soldiers dispatched again ahead of time

indicators.note: ahead of says the soldiers, sent out again, stand before the letter for time

parts.note: something dispatched a second time is re-sent
men is a term for ordinary soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Troops are angry at being sent back out earlier than planned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispatched again' is read as a hyphenated verb run into one word; 'ahead of' places it and the soldiers before the abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a feeling of grievance or ill will.
